heroHeadline: U.S. Solar Surpasses Wind as Largest Clean Source — 370+ GW Deployed; World Environment Day Calls for Faster Transition
heroSubtitle: 3,828 days since the Paris Agreement — The American Clean Power Association's Q1 2026 report (June 3) confirmed that utility-scale solar has surpassed wind as the largest installed clean power source in the United States, with 370+ GW of total clean capacity deployed and a record 6.4 GW added in Q1 2026 alone (led by 3.6 GW solar and 2.4 GW battery storage). The project pipeline surged to 195 GW. On World Environment Day 2026 (June 5, Baku), UNEP's #NowForClimate campaign declared the clean energy transformation 'inevitable' while calling for faster pace. Australia's Queensland grid hit a new instantaneous renewable record of 79.5% on May 31. MIT published research on flexible electrochemical carbon capture (EMCC) compatible with variable renewable electricity. UNFCCC SB64 pre-COP31 negotiations open in Bonn on June 8.
footerNote: Data sourced from IEA, IRENA, Ember, BloombergNEF, ACP, UNEP, and major international outlets. All figures reflect verified, publicly available data through June 2026.
